### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results. | # | Step | What to Do | Tips | |---|------|------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.).
• Set a budget (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, case, PSU, peripherals). | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to compare prices and check compatibility. | | 2 | **Gather Components** | • CPU (Intel/AMD)
• Motherboard (socket, chipset, form‑factor)
• RAM (DDR4/DDR5, speed, capacity)
• GPU (if not integrated)
• Storage (SSD/HDD, NVMe or SATA)
• Power Supply Unit (PSU, wattage, 80+ rating)
• Case (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX, size, airflow)
• Cooling (stock cooler, aftermarket air cooler, AIO liquid cooler)
• Operating System (Windows, Linux, etc.) | Check the motherboard’s CPU socket and RAM type. Verify PSU wattage with a PSU calculator. | | 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | • Clean, flat, static‑free surface.
• Anti‑static wrist strap (recommended).
• Screwdrivers (Phillips #0, #1). | Avoid carpet; use a static mat if possible. | | 4 | **Install the CPU** | 1. Open the CPU socket latch.
2. Align the CPU (gold triangle) with the socket.
3. Gently place it, then lock the latch. | Don’t force; the socket will guide. | | 5 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | • If cooler doesn’t have pre‑applied paste, apply a pea‑size amount on the CPU.
• Mount the cooler according to its instructions. | For AIO coolers, attach the pump to the motherboard header. | | 6 | **Insert RAM** | • Open the RAM slots’ clips.
• Align the notch on the RAM stick with the slot.
• Push firmly until the clips click. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel mode. | | 7 | **Mount the Motherboard** | 1. Place standoffs in the case (matching motherboard size).
2. Align the motherboard with the I/O shield.
3. Secure with screws. | Double‑check that all standoffs are correctly positioned. | | 8 | **Install Storage** | • For NVMe SSDs: slide into the M.2 slot, screw down.
• For SATA SSD/HDD: mount in drive bay, connect SATA data & power cables. | Label cables if you have many drives. | | 9 | **Install GPU** | 1. Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers from the case.
2. Insert GPU into the top PCIe x16 slot.
3. Secure with screws. | Connect required PCIe power connectors from PSU. | | 10 | **Connect Power Cables** | • 24‑pin ATX to motherboard.
• 8‑pin (or 4‑pin) CPU power.
• PCIe power to GPU.
• SATA power to drives.
• Front panel connectors (USB, audio, power button). | Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pin layout. | | 11 | **Cable Management** | • Route cables neatly behind the motherboard tray.
• Use zip ties or Velcro straps.
• Keep airflow unobstructed. | Good cable management improves airflow and makes future upgrades easier. | | 12 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | 1. Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
2. Power on.
3. Enter BIOS (usually Delete or F2).
4. Check that CPU, RAM, storage are detected.
5. Set boot priority to your OS drive. | Update BIOS if needed (check motherboard website). | | 13 | **Install Operating System** | • Create a bootable USB (Windows Media Creation Tool, Rufus, or Linux ISO).
• Boot from USB, follow installation prompts. | Install drivers after OS installation (GPU, chipset, Wi‑Fi). | | 14 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | • GPU driver (NVIDIA/AMD).
• Motherboard chipset driver.
• Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth driver.
• Windows updates. | Use manufacturer’s support site or driver update utilities. | | 15 | **Test & Benchmark** | • Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, Cinebench).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | Ensure temperatures stay within safe limits (CPU < 80 °C, GPU < 85 °C). | | 16 | **Final Touches** | • Add peripherals (monitor, keyboard, mouse).
• Configure power settings (sleep, hibernate).
• Backup system image. | Keep a spare USB drive for recovery. | --- #### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Short circuits** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; double‑check that no metal parts touch the motherboard. | | **Overheating** | Verify that the cooler is properly seated; ensure case fans are installed and oriented for intake/outlet. | | **Component incompatibility** | Use PCPartPicker’s “Check Compatibility” feature; read motherboard manual for supported CPUs/RAM. | | **Insufficient PSU** | Use an online PSU calculator; add 20–30 % headroom for future upgrades. | | **Boot failure** | Re‑check all power connections; ensure GPU is seated; verify BIOS settings (e.g., XMP profile for RAM). | --- #### Quick Reference: Motherboard Manual Highlights - **CPU Socket**: 1. Socket LGA1700 (Intel 12th/13th Gen), 2. AM4 (AMD Ryzen 3000/4000), 3. AM5 (Ryzen 7000). - **RAM Slots**: Dual‑channel (2 slots) or quad‑channel (4 slots). Install in matching pairs. - **PCIe Slots**: PCIe x16 (top) for GPU; PCIe x1 for expansion cards. - **SATA Ports**: Usually 4–6; connect to SATA data & power cables. - **M.2 Slots**: NVMe SSD; may share bandwidth with PCIe slots. - **Front Panel Header**: Power button, reset, USB, audio, LED indicators. --- #### Final Checklist - [ ] CPU seated correctly - [ ] Cooler installed & thermal paste applied - [ ] RAM installed in correct slots - [ ] Motherboard mounted on standoffs - [ ] GPU inserted & secured - [ ] All power cables connected - [ ] Front panel connectors attached - [ ] Cables managed & airflow clear - [ ] BIOS detects all components - [ ] OS installed & drivers updated - [ ] System runs stable under load Enjoy your new build! If you hit any snags, feel free to ask for help. Happy building!
